metadata.title: Game Theory on the Blockchain: A Model for Games with Smart Contracts
metadata.abstract: We propose a model for games in which the players have shared access to a blockchain that allows them to deploy smart contracts to act on their behalf. This changes fundamental game-theoretic assumptions about rationality since a contract can commit a player to act irrationally in specific subgames, making credible otherwise non-credible threats. This is further complicated by considering the interaction between multiple contracts which can reason about each other. This changes the nature of the game in a nontrivial way as choosing which contract to play can itself be considered a move in the game. Our model generalizes known notions of equilibria, with a single contract being equivalent to a Stackelberg equilibrium, and two contracts being equivalent to a reverse Stackelberg equilibrium. We prove a number of bounds on the complexity of computing SPE in such games with smart contracts. We show that computing an SPE is \(\textsf {PSPACE}\)-hard in the general case. Specifically, in games with k contracts, we show that computing an SPE is \(\varSigma _k^\textsf {P}\)-hard for games of imperfect information. We show that computing an SPE remains \(\textsf {PSPACE}\)-hard in games of perfect information if we allow for an unbounded number of contracts. We give an algorithm for computing an SPE in two-contract games of perfect information that runs in time \(O(m\ell )\) where m is the size of the game tree and \(\ell \) is the number of terminal nodes. Finally, we conjecture the problem to be \(\textsf {NP}\)-complete for three contracts.

editorial_review.scope: EconCS x Blockchain or cryptographic mechanism design/security
editorial_review.merit_reason: Author paper gives two-stage Bayesian games for proposer cheating, validator selection and validation effort, with explicit payoffs and mixed-strategy thresholds. This is substantive strategic participation beyond consensus engineering. Independent one-to-four leader games, assumed rationality, exogenous attack beliefs and proposer importance parameters constrain results; the importance estimator is not specified. Reward/penalty calibration and randomness assumptions do not establish universal honest behavior, decentralization or resistance to all attacks. Admit for the model contribution, without endorsing the title as a measured guarantee.
editorial_review.review_depth: Author manuscript first/second-stage Bayesian-game payoff tables and BNE derivations; formal GameSec metadata corroborated.

editorial_review.merit_reason: Publisher abstract and primary-indexed protocol description establish sealed-bid blockchain auction realization with binding/non-retractable bids and verifiable comparisons. This is cryptographic implementation of an economic mechanism. Its weaker-than-general-MPC model requires a semi-honest non-colluding judge and honest-majority opening after abort; order of bids leaks. Do not label it fully trustless, value-order hiding, or an incentive-compatible bidding-equilibrium theorem. Admit this user-selected contribution with bounded evidence; full proof review was unavailable due to IACR403.
